articles.title: Ilhan Omar's wealth scandal takes a turn just one day after raid of her DC home
articles.summary: Jeanine Pirro says her office is investigating Ilhan Omar's financial disclosures after business valuations tied to her husband surged dramatically.
articles.body:
U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro revealed Tuesday that her office is investigating Rep. Ilhan Omar's financial disclosures, opening a new chapter in the controversy surrounding the Minnesota Democrat's previously reported multimillion-dollar assets.

Speaking on Fox News' "America Reports," Pirro said her office was examining Omar's financial disclosures, which previously showed that the reported value of businesses tied to her husband, Tim Mynett, had surged from as much as $51,000 in 2023 to as much as $30 million in 2024.

The latest development comes one day after federal agents searched Omar's Washington, D.C., home as part of an ongoing criminal investigation involving her immigration paperwork, two sources familiar with the probe told Fox News Digital.

The Justice Department confirmed that Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant Monday as part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation. It remains unclear whether the search is connected in any way to the financial disclosure investigation described by Pirro.

The disclosures drew scrutiny from congressional Republicans, including House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, R-Ky., who requested financial records from two companies tied to Mynett in February.

The original filings, examined by Fox News Digital earlier this year, showed millions of dollars in newly reported assets associated with two of Mynett's business ventures — a California-based winery and a Washington, D.C.-based venture capital firm.

The winery, eStCru LLC, saw its reported valuation jump from between $15,000 and $50,000 in 2023 to between $1 million and $5 million in 2024. Rose Lake Capital LLC showed an even sharper increase, rising from a reported value of between $1 and $1,000 in 2023 to between $5 million and $25 million the following year.

Combined, the businesses had reported values ranging from approximately $15,000 to $51,000 in 2023, compared with between $6 million and $30 million in 2024.

Financial disclosure forms report assets in broad ranges rather than exact dollar amounts, meaning the filings did not establish the couple's precise net worth.

In February, Comer requested documents and communications related to the finances of eStCru LLC and Rose Lake Capital LLC, raising questions about the dramatic increase in their reported valuations.

Omar subsequently amended her financial disclosures in April , reducing the couple's combined reported assets to between $18,004 and $95,000. The revised filing listed her husband's two businesses as having no net value after accounting for liabilities.

Omar's office, at the time, said the original disclosures had failed to properly account for liabilities associated with her husband's businesses, creating what it described as a misleading picture of the couple's finances.

The congresswoman has repeatedly maintained that she is not a millionaire .

In September, the Office of Congressional Conduct voted 5-1 to recommend that the House Ethics Committee dismiss misconduct allegations stemming from the financial disclosures.

The congressional watchdog found there was not substantial reason to believe Omar had reported false or incomplete information in violation of federal law or House rules.

Omar's office characterized the findings as vindication, maintaining that the congresswoman had done nothing wrong.

The congressional watchdog's review is separate from the federal investigation described by Pirro on Tuesday.

Omar's latest annual financial disclosure, filed in May, listed assets totaling between approximately $20,000 and $125,000, according to a Minnesota Star Tribune analysis. The filing also reported student loan and credit card debt associated with her husband.

The Somali-born congresswoman has denied allegations of wrongdoing and has accused the Trump administration of targeting her for political reasons — especially after Monday's raid of her Washington, D.C., residence.

The Minnesota Democrat has been a frequent target of criticism from President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans.

articles.title: Tim Walz warns Democrats will face reckoning if they win power and fail to deliver change
articles.summary: Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz warns Democrats will face serious backlash if they win back power but fail to deliver on housing and college education.
articles.body:
Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz issued a warning to his party in an interview Thursday, arguing there would be backlash if Democrats win elections in November and beyond but fail to make significant structural changes.

During an interview with "The Lever" founder David Sirota, Walz was asked if the Democratic Party had an issue offering up big promises but ultimately failing to deliver.

"Yes, a hundred percent. It's a hundred percent," Walz said. "I always use the line, as I said, we win these elections not to bank the political capital to win the next one but to improve lives. We're too slow about it. And some of that is structural,"

He pointed to former Sen. Joe Manchin's position that the filibuster must remain in place in the Senate.

"Look, I'm friends with Joe Manchin, but the desire to hold onto the filibuster at all costs as an institution when it had real impacts on people's lives of real important things, and by not doing that, it played right into the hands of the Republicans. I think we're not responsive, and then we fall into that 'But we voted for you, and you didn't get anything done,'" Walz said.

Manchin has been consistent in his support for the filibuster. In 2022, he and then-Sen. Kyrsten Sinema voted against changing the Senate's 60-vote threshold for advancing most legislation, opposing other Democrats who sought to change the rules to pass voting legislation.

Walz, the 2024 Democratic vice presidential nominee, warned of a "real danger."

"Here's where I think the real danger is. If there is not significant structural change — whether it's inequities, you know, income inequities or opportunities — the backlash, because, I said this: I got into politics because I said we'll never find a worse president than George Bush . And I think now, if you think that this is the pinnacle of how bad things can get, I would caution you to rethink that.

"And especially if Democrats do all of this, the public turns out, they vote for us and kids still can't afford a college education, can't afford housing. That's going to be a problem."

He then predicted that Democrats would regain control of the House, Senate and eventually the presidency in 2028 .

Lindsey Drath, CEO of the Forward Party, told Fox News Digital, "We shouldn't advocate for abolishing the filibuster to drive home party-line votes with no effort to advance cross-partisan consensus law making. What hampers Congress' ability to deliver material solutions to the American people is a two-party system that penalizes working across the aisle.

"This circular dynamic, whereby Democrats or Republicans enter into a narrow majority, only to focus on maintaining power, accumulates a kind of figurative debt against the challenges facing the American people," she said. "This dynamic pushes our elected officials away from working on real solutions for actual problems and toward whatever hyper polarized means by which they can to hold on to power.

"This is why a fulcrum strategy is key," Drath continued. "The Senate today passes almost nothing on a bipartisan basis, not because the problems aren't solvable, but because neither party has any incentive to negotiate. Every compromise is a political cost. If someone crosses the aisle, they are attacked by their party. It is framed as every deal made is a loss to play at home. The incentive is to obstruct, posture and wait for the next election.

"The fulcrum strategy is that you don't need a majority to change the Senate," she added. "You need only a handful. It uses a small bloc of independents to balance power in Congress and take away full majority from either side. With an expected closely divided Congress this cycle, this is very relevant and real. It would mean both parties would have to negotiate with those few in the middle before anything passes. The party that wants their vote has to offer something real, something that actually serves the people."

Walz announced in January that he would not seek elected office again after previously announcing he wouldn't run for a third term as governor.

He reflected on his tenure as governor in a September interview, including his handling of widespread fraud involving Minnesota social services programs.

"Fraud — should have stopped it sooner," Walz told The Minnesota Star Tribune . "We didn't stop them. I accept that. I think there does need to be accountability with that. And part of it is that, yep, that's with me, I'll step aside."

The governor said the state "immediately" took action to address the fraud and then suggested that the true cost of the fraud, estimated at $9 billion by federal prosecutors, has been overstated. Walz also compared the fraud losses to the cost of President Donald Trump's White House ballroom , which he suggested was more expensive.

"I should have been down on those agencies a little more, but I will tell you this, in the scheme of things, all the fraud that's been prosecuted, by the way, and all the fraud that's probably out there is less than the ballroom at the White House," Walz said.

"So, it puts it into perspective. It doesn't make it right. Doesn't make it right."

Fox News' Andrew Mark Miller contributed to this report.

articles.title: Katie Zacharia calls herself a lawyer. Legal experts aren't sure.
articles.summary: Katie Zacharia made her debut as President Donald Trump's new White House press secretary Tuesday morning, breaking news (announcing that Kimberly Guilfoyle...
articles.body:
Katie Zacharia made her debut as President Donald Trump's new White House press secretary Tuesday morning, breaking news (announcing that Kimberly Guilfoyle had been asked to resign as ambassador to Greece) and sparking commentary about her performance (Trump, for one, said he "thought she was very good").

But Zacharia has also made news, regarding how she has represented herself and her résumé in public appearances.

"What state did she pass the bar exam in?" a journalist shouted at Trump on Tuesday morning as he walked to Marine One. The president leaned in. Zacharia stood behind him. "She said she's an attorney," the journalist repeated. "Where did she pass the bar exam? Which state?"

Trump stepped aside to let Zacharia answer: "When I moved to China," she appeared to say through muffled audio.

Journalist Judd Legum, who writes the Popular Information newsletter, identified numerous occasions when Zacharia appeared on national media outlets citing her credentials as a lawyer. He counted 18 appearances on Fox News Channel when she made such mentions, and he found that she also called herself a lawyer on her social media accounts.

Zacharia graduated with a law degree from Pepperdine University, but Legum wrote that he could not find that she passed any state's bar exam, which is almost always a requirement for practicing law in the United States.

The Washington Post conducted its own review and also could not find any active or expired bar admissions under Zacharia's name, including her maiden name, Black.

Zacharia graduated from Pepperdine with a bachelor's degree in 2007 and a law degree in 2011, the university confirmed in an email Tuesday. She then worked as an associate on the international practice team at the law firm Zhong Lun in Beijing, from 2011 until 2013, according to her LinkedIn profile.

Her only other legal role was as general counsel of Fix California, a group started by Trump administration official Richard Grenell, from 2024 to 2025. Representatives of Zhong Lun and Fix California did not respond to requests for comment.

The White House did not provide evidence that Zacharia has been a licensed lawyer in the United States, but said in a statement that she "worked on international transaction law" in China and "practiced international transactional law, with all the appropriate credentials."

Several legal ethics experts said that if a person is not a licensed lawyer but is identifying as one, that presents serious ethical and legal problems.

"A J.D. degree does not make you a lawyer," said Stephen Gillers, a professor at New York University School of Law.

Bruce A. Green, the director of the Louis Stein Center for Law and Ethics at Fordham University School of Law, agreed. "A law school graduate is just that - a law school graduate," he said.

A person is considered a lawyer or an attorney only after being admitted to practice law, Green said, adding that in most states, this requires passing a bar exam and demonstrating proper character.

Leonard M. Niehoff, a professor at the University of Michigan Law School, said that there is a "world of difference" between having a law degree and being a licensed attorney. And, he said, there could be consequences for falsely claiming to be a licensed attorney.

"Many, if not all, states have statutes that prohibit the unauthorized practice of law, which commonly includes falsely holding oneself out as a licensed attorney for purposes of monetary gain," Niehoff said. "Making false or misleading statements about being licensed as an attorney therefore raises not just serious ethical issues but legal ones."

Even if Zacharia were licensed in another country, Green said, her public statements in U.S. media would still be misleading if she did not say that she's not licensed in the United States.

"Someone in the U.S. who just flat-out calls themselves a lawyer, without further qualification or explanation, will mislead listeners or readers to think that they are permitted to practice law here in the U.S. - which they are not," he said.

Zacharia resides in California, according to public records. In a statement Tuesday, a spokesman for the State Bar of California said that it "has no record of Kate Sharon Zacharia or Kate Sharon Black having been licensed to practice law in California." The spokesman also said there are no records under Katie, her nickname.

The spokesman said that as a general matter, "California Business and Professions section 6126 makes it unlawful for anyone who is not an active licensee of the State Bar, or otherwise authorized pursuant to statute or court rule to practice law in California, to advertise or hold themselves out as practicing or entitled to practice law in California."

And even if Zacharia worked for a law firm in China, she probably would not have been admitted to the bar there, given that country's requirements, experts in Chinese law said.

"She could not have passed the PRC [People's Republic of China] bar exam, either, since you have to be a PRC national to take it," said Donald C. Clarke, a professor at George Washington University Law School who specializes in Chinese law.

Clarke said that firms like Zhong Lun, which he called reputable, can hire foreigners to do certain tasks and can determine whether to require an employee to have passed a foreign bar exam.

"But the person still would not be allowed do anything that required a PRC or foreign bar qualification to do," he said, including representing clients in Chinese court.

Lester Ross, senior counsel at the law firm WilmerHale, also said the Chinese bar exam is available only to Chinese citizens. "A foreign national who has passed the bar in a foreign jurisdiction may practice the law of such jurisdiction in China and provide his or her understanding of Chinese law, but may not practice Chinese law," he said.

Isaac Arnsdorf and Aaron Schaffer contributed to this report.

articles.title: Lula ouve de aliados que PEC da Segurança será votada antes do 2º turno e que governo tem votos para aprovar fim da 6x1 | G1
articles.standfirst: Petista ligou para presidente da CCJ para agradecer pela votação do texto que amplia a participação da União na segurança pública. Líder do governo no Senado pediu a parlamentares da base que participem de sessão sobre redução da jornada de trabalho.
articles.summary: Petista ligou para presidente da CCJ para agradecer pela votação do texto que amplia a participação da União na segurança pública. Líder do governo no Senado pediu a parlamentares da base que participem de sessão sobre redução da jornada de trabalho.
articles.body:
Após a conclusão da aprovação da PEC da Segurança na Comissão de Constituição e Justiça (CCJ) do Senado , o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) ligou para o senador Otto Alencar ( PSD -BA), que preside o colegiado, para agradecer pela aprovação.

Lula ouviu do parlamentar que a proposta que amplia a participação da União na segurança deve ser votada no plenário do Senado antes do segundo turno das eleições e, possivelmente, ainda nesta semana, em um movimento liderado pelo presidente da Casa, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP).

Segundo apurou o g1 , o líder do MDB , senador Eduardo Braga (AM) está trabalhando nos bastidores para conseguir assinaturas para a aprovação de um calendário especial para acelerar a tramitação da matéria .

Para aprovar uma PEC, o regimento do Senado prevê que o texto seja debatido em cinco sessões. Após a aprovação em primeiro turno, é preciso esperar mais cinco dias úteis e três sessões para votar em segundo turno.

Com a aprovação de um calendário especial, não está descartado que Alcolumbre convoque uma sessão para esta quinta-feira (15) para votar a PEC da Segurança.

Ao falar com Lula, Otto Alencar garantiu que a PEC será aprovada. Ao g1 , o parlamentar lembrou que o presidente irá recriar Ministério da Segurança Publica até semana que vem.

Governo confiante na aprovação do fim da 6x1

Em outra frente, o governo está confiante na aprovação da PEC que acaba com a escala de trabalho 6x1. A s essão de votação está marcada para a tarde desta quarta-feira , em formato semipresencial, o que permite aos senadores votar sem estar em Brasília.

A líder do governo no Senado, Teresa Leitão (PT), pediu que todos os senadores da base governista compareçam ao plenário para reforçar a posição de apoio à proposta.

O ministro das Relações Institucionais, José Guimarães, pretende acompanhar a votação no Senado.

Segundo o ministro, a data da promulgação será definida pela cúpula do Congresso, mas a expectativa é que o procedimento seja concluído rapidamente.

“Será promulgada imediatamente. Acredito que entre quinta e sexta-feira já esteja resolvido”, disse Guimarães.

Lula celebra votação e critica adversários

Em uma rede social, Lula divulgou um vídeo em que diz que "finalmente o povo vai conquistar o fim da escala 6x1.

Ele criticou a mudança de postura de adversários em relação ao texto. Nesta terça (13), Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, que era crítico à PEC em debate no Congresso, declarou voto a favor da proposta.

"É importante ter em conta que os nossos adversários decidiram ontem [terça] que vão votar favorável. Mas é preciso ficar alerta, eles querem votar por oportunismo eleitoral. Mas essa gente não tardará, se algum dia acontecer de eles ganharem o Brasil, de acabar, porque eles preferem o sistema do Javier Milei [presidente da Argentina], de 12 horas por dia de trabalho", afirmou Lula.

articles.title: Flávio foca em segurança e Lula no fim 6x1 em horário eleitoral | G1
articles.standfirst: Propaganda de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) destacou propostas para a segurança pública e criticou a pichação de uma estação de metrô durante ato pró-Lula no domingo (11), em São Paulo. Lula (PT) dedicou a maior parte do horário eleitoral ao fim da escala 6x1 e ao "Prospera MEI", anunciado na terça-feira (13).
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula detalharam propostas de segurança e o fim da escala 6x1, incluindo o Prospera MEI, no horário eleitoral desta quarta-feira.
articles.body:
Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) durante propaganda eleitoral gratuita nesta quarta-feira (14). — Foto: Reprodução

O horário eleitoral gratuito desta quarta-feira (14) teve uma configuração diferente, com a exibição de dois programas do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), candidato à Presidência, intercalados pela propaganda do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que disputa a reeleição.

Flávio abriu o horário eleitoral com um programa inédito e voltou a aparecer após a propaganda de Lula, desta vez com a reexibição de uma peça que havia ido ao ar sem áudio na segunda-feira (12) , feriado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, devido a uma falha técnica. A reapresentação, agora com som, foi determinada pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) .

Nos dois programas exibidos nesta quarta-feira, Flávio Bolsonaro abordou, respectivamente, propostas para a segurança pública e a economia. Já o presidente Lula dedicou a maior parte de sua propaganda à defesa do fim da escala 6x1, cuja votação está prevista para a tarde desta quarta-feira no Senado .

No primeiro programa, inédito, Flávio concentrou o discurso na segurança pública. Entre as propostas, voltou a mencionar o Smart Brasil , iniciativa que consta do plano de governo registrado na Justiça Eleitoral com o nome Muralha Brasileira.

O plano previa a compra de 1 milhão de câmeras de reconhecimento facial, integradas a bancos de dados criminais. Na propaganda desta quarta-feira, porém, Flávio ampliou a proposta para 2 milhões de câmeras.

O candidato também defendeu a entrada do Brasil no chamado Escudo das Américas, coalizão lançada pelo governo Donald Trump, dos EUA, e que reúne governos alinhados a seu governo na América Latina para o combate a facções criminosas. A proposta não consta no plano de governo de Flávio Bolsonaro registrado na Justiça Eleitoral.

Ao final, o candidato do PL também criticou manifestantes que participaram de um ato pró-Lula em São Paulo, no domingo (11), após uma estação de metrô ser alvo de pichações e ter vidros danificados.

A peça reexibida de Flávio comemorou o Dia de Nossa Senhora Aparecida e tratou de propostas voltadas à economia, já exibidas em programas eleitorais anteriores. A peça contou com depoimentos de Daniella Marques, uma das coordenadoras da campanha, e de aliados como Tereza Cristina (PP-MS), Michelle Bolsonaro (PL-DF), Augusto Cury (Avante) e Ronaldo Caiado (PSD).

Lula destaca fim da escala 6x1 e Prospera MEI

O programa de Lula começou com ataques a Flávio Bolsonaro. A propaganda comparou o adversário a uma maçã podre com larvas.

A campanha petista mostrou também imagens de manifestações realizadas no último fim de semana em cidades como São Paulo. A peça também explorou a presença de Lula nas redes sociais, com vídeos no formato selfie gravados pelo presidente, que disputa a reeleição, neste 2º turno.

O principal tema do programa, porém, foi o fim da escala de trabalho 6x1, que será votada no Senado nesta quarta (14).

A peça apresentou relatos de trabalhadores sobre as dificuldades de conciliar emprego, lazer e qualificação profissional. A campanha sustenta que Lula é o candidato que vai garantir a plena aprovação e implantação da proposta.

Outro destaque da campanha do petista foi o Prospera MEI, pacote de benefícios apresentado pelo governo federal na última terça-feira (13) .

Entre as medidas anunciadas no programa eleitoral, estão o aumento do teto de faturamento anual para R$ 140 mil, a possibilidade de contratação de até dois funcionários e a concessão de até R$ 5 mil não reembolsáveis via PIX para investimentos.

articles.title: TV Globo faz entrevistas e debate com candidatos à Presidência | G1
articles.standfirst: Encontros serão exibidos ao vivo pela TV Globo, com transmissão simultânea pela GloboNews e pelo g. Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) será entrevistado no dia 15 de outubro, e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), no dia 16.
articles.summary: Encontros serão exibidos ao vivo pela TV Globo, com transmissão simultânea pela GloboNews e pelo g. Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) será entrevistado no dia 15 de outubro, e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), no dia 16.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula em programa eleitoral na TV — Foto: Reprodução

A TV Globo promove, nos dias 15 e 16 de outubro, entrevistas ao vivo com os candidatos que disputam o segundo turno da eleição presidencial.

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) será entrevistado no dia 15 de outubro , e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), no dia 16. A ordem foi definida por sorteio realizado em reunião com representantes das campanhas.

Realizados nos Estúdios Globo, no Rio de Janeiro , os encontros serão conduzidos por Renata Lo Prete e exibidos na TV Globo após o ‘Jornal Nacional’, com transmissão simultânea pela GloboNews e pelo g1. Após a exibição, o conteúdo ficará disponível na íntegra no Globoplay e no g1.

As entrevistas integram a cobertura para o segundo turno das Eleições 2026 e têm como principal objetivo oferecer aos brasileiros a oportunidade de conhecer e avaliar as propostas dos candidatos para os desafios do país.

Quando será o debate de presidenciáveis na Globo?

No dia 23 de outubro, a TV Globo realiza o último debate entre os dois candidatos que disputam a Presidência da República. Foram convidados Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). O encontro acontecerá nos Estúdios Globo, no Rio de Janeiro, logo após o ‘Jornal Nacional’.

Mediado pelo jornalista César Tralli, o debate será transmitido ao vivo pela TV Globo, e também poderá ser acompanhado simultaneamente pela GloboNews e pelo g1.

articles.title: Deputado do PT pede ao STF investigação e afastamento de Nunes Marques do comando do TSE | G1
articles.standfirst: Rui Falcão afirma que é preciso investigar se informações falsas ou imprecisas foram usadas para tirar do ar o canal 'Exército do Lula'.
articles.summary: Rui Falcão afirma que é preciso investigar se informações falsas ou imprecisas foram usadas para tirar do ar o canal 'Exército do Lula'.
articles.body:
O deputado federal Rui Falcão (PT-SP) pediu ao Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) que investigue a atuação de Kassio Nunes Marques , presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), e de integrantes da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no caso que levou à suspensão do canal de WhatsApp “Exército do Lula”.

No documento enviado ao STF, Rui Falcão afirma que é preciso investigar se informações falsas ou diferentes do que mostravam os documentos do processo foram apresentadas pela campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro ou incluídas nas decisões de Nunes Marques.

Juridicamente, a suspeita apontada pelo deputado é de falsidade ideológica eleitoral.

O deputado também pede que Nunes Marques seja afastado temporariamente do TSE enquanto o caso é analisado. O pedido não envolve o afastamento do ministro do STF.

A representação está ligada à disputa em torno do “Exército do Lula”, canal de WhatsApp administrado pelo deputado federal André Janones (Rede-MG) e utilizado para divulgar mensagens a apoiadores do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

Nos últimos dias, o canal foi alvo de decisões diferentes dentro do TSE após a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro pedir sua suspensão.

No domingo (11), Nunes Marques determinou que o canal fosse tirado do ar. Horas depois, o corregedor-geral eleitoral, Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, derrubou essa decisão e permitiu que o canal voltasse a funcionar.

Na segunda (12), uma análise técnica do TSE examinou as publicações disponíveis e não identificou a reprodução dos conteúdos falsos apontados no processo.

Já na terça (13), Nunes Marques determinou que o canal só poderia funcionar depois de ser formalmente registrado na Justiça Eleitoral. A campanha de Lula fez o registro no mesmo dia.

Na noite de terça, o canal estava fora do ar. Nunes Marques afirmou que ele poderia voltar a funcionar depois do prazo de 48 horas previsto pelas regras citadas pelo TSE.

Ex-presidente do Partido do Trabalhadores (PT), Rui Falcão, hoje deputado. Imagem de 2016. — Foto: Vanessa Carvalho/Brazil Photo Press/Estadão Conteúdo

Por que Rui Falcão quer uma investigação?

Um dos principais questionamentos do deputado é sobre quais provas a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro apresentou para conseguir a suspensão do canal.

Segundo a representação, a campanha afirmou ter documentos para mostrar como mensagens e vídeos circularam pelo “Exército do Lula”.

Rui Falcão pede que o STF confira esses documentos para saber se eles realmente comprovam o que foi alegado.

O deputado também pede que seja verificada outra afirmação feita pela campanha: a de que teriam sido apresentadas centenas de denúncias contra o canal sem que nenhuma providência visível tivesse sido tomada.

Para Rui Falcão, é preciso verificar quantas denúncias efetivamente existiram, quando foram feitas e como foram tratadas.

Outro ponto questionado é a afirmação de que parte importante do conteúdo divulgado pelo canal já havia sido considerada falsa pelo TSE. Rui Falcão quer que os investigadores comparem as mensagens do canal com as decisões anteriores do tribunal.

A representação usa ainda como argumento uma análise técnica feita pelo próprio TSE depois da primeira decisão de Nunes Marques.

O levantamento examinou as publicações disponíveis do canal entre 2 e 11 de outubro e não encontrou novas publicações reproduzindo as afirmações que já tinham sido analisadas pelo tribunal.

O próprio documento de Rui Falcão, entretanto, registra uma limitação dessa análise: os vídeos não foram transcritos por causa da urgência do trabalho.

Por isso, a representação não afirma que a análise técnica, sozinha, prove que Nunes Marques usou informação falsa.

O pedido é para que o STF compare o material disponível com as afirmações feitas no processo e nas decisões.

Outro ponto que Rui Falcão pede que seja investigado é a forma como a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro apresentou seus pedidos ao TSE.

Segundo a representação, Cueva analisava uma ação da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro e havia pedido mais informações antes de decidir se suspendia o canal.

Quarenta e um minutos depois dessa decisão, a campanha levou à Presidência do TSE outro pedido relacionado à suspensão do “Exército do Lula”.

Depois, o corregedor-geral afirmou que caminhos diferentes dentro do tribunal não poderiam ser usados para permitir a escolha sucessiva de quem decidiria a questão.

A própria representação de Rui Falcão, porém, ressalva que Cueva também afirmou que essa sequência de acontecimentos não permitia concluir, por si só, que a campanha tivesse agido com uma intenção específica.

Por que Rui Falcão pede o afastamento de Nunes Marques

Além da investigação, Rui Falcão quer que Nunes Marques seja temporariamente afastado das funções que exerce no TSE.

O deputado sustenta que as decisões tomadas pelo ministro beneficiaram a candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro e prejudicaram a comunicação de apoiadores de Lula.

O afastamento pedido seria limitado às funções eleitorais de Nunes Marques e iria até a diplomação dos eleitos. O deputado não pede que ele deixe o cargo de ministro do STF.

Rui Falcão também quer que o próprio TSE analise se Nunes Marques pode continuar atuando nos processos relacionados às duas candidaturas.

m termos simples, o deputado quer que o tribunal avalie se o ministro mantém a imparcialidade necessária para decidir questões dessa disputa eleitoral.

O que Rui Falcão quer que seja investigado

Entre as medidas solicitadas ao STF estão:

conferir se os documentos apresentados pela campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro comprovavam a circulação no canal dos conteúdos citados;

verificar quantas denúncias contra o “Exército do Lula” foram realmente feitas à Meta e qual foi o resultado delas;

comparar as mensagens do canal com decisões anteriores do TSE;

identificar quem produziu as informações apresentadas em nome da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro;

analisar documentos, registros de tramitação e informações técnicas relacionadas às decisões sobre o canal.

O pedido agora depende da análise do STF.

articles.title: Janones pede que Nunes Marques libere canal 'Exército do Lula' | G1
articles.standfirst: Nesta terça, presidente do TSE definiu prazo de 48 horas após o registro feito pela candidatura de Lula para retomada do canal de WhatsApp. Para defesa de Janones, suspensão não deveria ser aplicada.
articles.summary: A defesa de Janones solicitou ao TSE a liberação imediata do canal Exército do Lula no WhatsApp, contestando o prazo de 48 horas imposto por Nunes Marques.
articles.body:
A defesa do deputado federal André Janones ( Rede -MG) apresentou um pedido de reconsideração ao presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), ministro Kassio Nunes Marques , para que seja revista a decisão que manteve a suspensão temporária do canal de mensagens "Exército do Lula ", no WhatsApp .

Os advogados solicitam o restabelecimento imediato da ferramenta, com liberação para envio de atualizações e ingresso de novos seguidores.

Nesta terça, Nunes Marques reconheceu o registro do canal pela campanha de Lula e estabeleceu que a ferramenta só poderia voltar a funcionar após o prazo de 48 horas previsto em uma resolução do TSE .

O registro foi feito após uma exigência de Nunes Marques determinada depois que a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ) acionou a Justiça Eleitoral contra o canal, apontando disseminação de desinformação.

📱Coordenado por Janones, o canal 'Exército do Lula' tem mais de 4 milhões de inscritos no WhatsApp. O objetivo é compartilhar áudios, vídeos e orientações para apoiadores do presidente Lula.

No pedido apresentado na Justiça Eleitoral, a defesa de Janones afirma que o canal é de iniciativa autônoma de apoiadores, o que, na avaliação dos advogados, dispensaria a exigência de comunicação formal prévia à Justiça Eleitoral.

Os advogados também apontam que, independentemente da desobrigação legal, o canal foi formalmente cadastrado e informado no registro de candidatura do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), cumprindo requisito formal estabelecido pela Corte.

A defesa de Janones também afirma que a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) mantém "robusta e massiva estrutura de canais" no WhatsApp para distribuir propaganda, mas que não houve restrições da Justiça Eleitoral para o candidato do PL.

Entre os canais listados está o "Tropa do Flávio BR", que foi registrado pela campanha , mas não precisou ficar 48 horas fora do ar, segundo os advogados.

Outro canal citado é o mantido pelo deputado Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG), apoiador de Flávio. Os advogados criticam o fato de que o deputado reeleito do PL não precisou fazer o registro de seu canal no TSE.

"[Nikolas Ferreira e outros políticos] mantêm canais com dezenas de milhares de inscritos no WhatsApp e dezenas de milhões de seguidores nas redes, distribuindo ostensivamente propaganda eleitoral da chapa de Flávio Bolsonaro, sem que esses canais jamais tenham sido declarados no registro de candidatura e sem sofrerem nenhuma medida restritiva de funcionamento", dizem os advogados de Janones.

Se a decisão de Nunes Marques não for reconsiderada pelo próprio ministro, a defesa pede o envio do caso ao plenário do TSE, em caráter de urgência, para análise na próxima sessão da Corte Eleitoral.

Em outra frente, os advogados de Janones também acionaram o corregedor do TSE, ministro Villas Bôas Cueva. Eles entendem que cabe a Cueva analisar os pedidos relacionados ao canal "Exército do Lula" e não a Nunes Marques.

Dep. André Janones (Rede-MG) — Foto: Mario Agra / Câmara dos Deputados

articles.title: André Janones nega fake news e aciona advogada de Flávio Bolsonaro | G1
articles.standfirst: Em entrevista ao Estúdio i, deputado afirmou que apagou mensagens de mobilização após o cumprimento de “missões”, mas que nenhuma delas continha informações falsas. Ele também criticou a decisão que exige o registro do canal Exército do Lula.
articles.summary: André Janones nega fake news no canal Exército do Lula e anuncia processo por calúnia contra a advogada da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro após acusações.
articles.body:
O deputado André Janones (Rede - MG) afirmou nesta quarta-feira (14), em entrevista ao Estúdio i , da GloboNews , que não divulgou fake news no canal “Exército do Lula ” e que seus advogados vão acionar por calúnia a advogada da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Maria Cláudia Bucchianeri.

A declaração foi uma resposta à entrevista concedida pela advogada ao programa , antes da participação do deputado. Ela afirmou que o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) não identificou fake news no canal porque Janones havia apagado os posts .

“A doutora cometeu um crime. Os advogados meus já irão acioná-la porque ela afirmou que eu pratiquei crimes que eu não pratiquei. Isso chama calúnia”, disse o deputado.

Maria Cláudia afirmou que a equipe jurídica da campanha de Flávio incluiu, no relatório que deve entregar ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), provas de que o deputado, responsável pelo grupo Exército do Lula no WhatsApp, disseminou fake news na plataforma.

O parlamentar confirmou que excluiu mensagens. Segundo ele, porém, as publicações continham orientações para mobilizar apoiadores, como chamadas para ampliar o número de participantes do canal ou de seguidores de perfis ligados à esquerda.

Janones explicou que apaga parte dessas publicações depois que as ações, que chama de “missões”, são concluídas, para facilitar o acesso dos novos integrantes aos conteúdos mais recentes.

“Quando essa missão é cumprida, eu apago esse áudio porque eu não vou perder o tempo dos novos membros ouvindo algo que não faz mais sentido”, afirmou.

O parlamentar também criticou a determinação de registrar o Exército do Lula na Justiça Eleitoral. O registro ocorreu após uma série de impasses e embates jurídicos envolvendo o canal de WhatsApp na Corte.

Na avaliação do administrador do canal, a exigência é ilegal porque ele não é candidato à Presidência. O deputado disse que cumpriu a ordem para evitar que o canal fosse retirado do ar.

“A gente está vendo a censura acontecer diante dos nossos olhos, devagarinho. A gente está vendo uma ditadura começando a se instalar no nosso país”, afirmou.

O deputado acusou tratamento desigual entre as campanhas de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro. Como comparação, citou os grupos e a atuação digital do deputado Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG), aliado do candidato do PL. O canal de WhatsApp administrado pelo parlamentar mineiro foi criado em resposta à iniciativa de Janones.

Questionado sobre uma reunião prevista para as 16h no TSE para discutir a volta do canal, Janones disse que será representado por seus advogados e rejeitou a possibilidade de um acordo com a parte adversária.

“A gente não quer acordo com essa gente. A gente quer que a Justiça prevaleça”, afirmou.

Críticas à comunicação da campanha de Lula

Durante a entrevista, Janones também afirmou que a campanha de Lula demorou a reconhecer a importância das redes sociais na disputa eleitoral. Disse ainda que foi criticado por alertar sobre o avanço de Flávio Bolsonaro.

“Na verdade, eles não me ignoravam. Se me ignorassem, já seria um ponto positivo. Eu era criticado, atacado muito por falar isso”, declarou.

Apesar da avaliação, o deputado afirmou que ainda há tempo para a campanha reagir e que “a reeleição de Lula tomou um caminho da vitória que é praticamente irreversível”.

articles.title: Advogada de Flávio Bolsonaro diz que Janones apagou fake news do canal | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo Maria Cláudia Bucchianeri, a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro está "espelhando em tempo real" o canal criado pelo deputado federal André Janones, para gravar conteúdos que venham a ser excluídos depois.
articles.summary: A advogada Maria Cláudia Bucchianeri afirma que o canal Exército do Lula é espelhado em tempo real para identificar fake news apagadas antes da análise do TSE.
articles.body:
A advogada Maria Cláudia Bucchianeri, responsável jurídica pela campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro, afirmou nesta quarta-feira (14), em entrevista ao Estúdio i, da GloboNews, que a área técnica do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) não identificou conteúdos falsos no canal "Exército do Lula", administrado pelo deputado federal André Janones, porque parte das mensagens havia sido apagada.

Segundo Bucchianeri, Janones excluiu 499 das 1.372 mensagens publicadas no canal, o equivalente a mais de um terço do conteúdo. A advogada afirmou que as publicações apagadas haviam sido encaminhadas 116 mil vezes antes da exclusão.

"Na verdade, a área técnica não disse que não tem [fake news]. Disse que não identificou. Ela disse que não achou. E ela não achou por um motivo muito simples: o Janones apagou um terço das mensagens que ele colocou naquele grupo", declarou.

Em entrevista ao Estúdio i, logo depois que a advogada falou, Janones negou ter postado fake news no canal e disse que vai acionar a advogada por calúnia.

Dep. André Janones (REDE - MG) — Foto: Mario Agra / Câmara dos Deputados

Bucchianeri disse que a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro pediu que a ação de investigação judicial eleitoral (Aije) contra o canal tramitasse inicialmente sob sigilo, para permitir a preservação das mensagens antes que os responsáveis fossem notificados.

De acordo com a advogada, a intenção era que a Justiça determinasse à Meta a conservação de todo o material publicado no canal. O pedido, no entanto, não foi acolhido.

"O ministro corregedor não determinou a conservação do material e tirou o sigilo. Então, quando isso foi parar na unidade técnica, não surpreendeu absolutamente ninguém que aquilo não fosse encontrado", afirmou.

A advogada afirmou que a equipe de Flávio Bolsonaro instalou um programa para registrar as publicações do canal em tempo real, incluindo conteúdos posteriormente excluídos, e disse que o material já foi apresentado ao TSE.

"A gente está espelhando em tempo real o canal do Janones. Nós temos a grande maioria das mensagens que ele apagou", disse.

Questionada sobre exemplos das supostas notícias falsas, a advogada citou publicações que acusariam ministros de receber propina e conteúdos relacionados à padroeira do Brasil.

Bucchianeri também acusou Janones de orientar integrantes do canal a compartilhar mensagens rapidamente, antes que fossem excluídas, e a adotar estratégias para evitar mecanismos de controle das plataformas.

A advogada afirmou ainda que o deputado orientava os participantes a copiar e colar conteúdos, em vez de encaminhá-los diretamente, e a compartilhar vídeos sem assisti-los, como forma de ampliar o engajamento.

A análise técnica do TSE, contudo, não identificou conteúdos apontados como irregulares.

Bucchianeri afirmou que a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro pode concordar com o restabelecimento do "Exército do Lula", sem a necessidade de aguardar o prazo de 48 horas após o registro do canal no TSE, caso as medidas determinadas pela Justiça Eleitoral sejam cumpridas.

Segundo a advogada, entre as medidas estão o monitoramento do canal e a proibição de apagar novas publicações, sob risco de derrubada do espaço.

"A gente pode concordar com o restabelecimento desse Exército do Lula, sem precisar cumprir a carência de 48 horas, porque agora, sim, o canal está no eixo", afirmou.

Bucchianeri também criticou o que considera uma falha na regulamentação do TSE sobre o uso de aplicativos de mensagens durante as eleições. Para ela, as restrições impostas aos grupos de WhatsApp não acompanharam o surgimento dos canais, que permitem alcançar públicos maiores.

articles.title: Lula assina Marco Legal dos Games e alerta sobre programas sociais | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente deu a declaração durante cerimônia no Palácio do Planalto sobre regulamentação do Marco Legal dos Jogos Eletrônicos. Campanha petista tem dito que Flávio cortará programas sociais se for eleito, o que candidato do PL nega.
articles.summary: Ao regulamentar o Marco Legal dos Jogos Eletrônicos, Lula alertou que programas sociais podem ser destruídos rapidamente e pediu que os jovens defendam suas conquistas.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) afirmou nesta quarta-feira (14) que, na política, "tem maluco pra tudo" e que, para elaborar um programa em uma gestão, é "difícil" porque demanda participação de vários setores, mas que, para "destruir" uma política pública, basta "um passo".

O petista deu a declaração a 11 dias do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, no qual concorre contra o candidato do PL, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Ele discursou durante a cerimônia de regulamentação do Marco Legal dos Jogos Eletrônicos no Palácio do Planalto.

A campanha de Lula tem afirmado que, se eleito, o filho de Jair Bolsonaro vai acabar com programas sociais criados em governos petistas, como o Pé-de-Meia; o Minha Casa, Minha Vida ; e o Farmácia Popular – o que Flávio nega.

Ao discursar no evento no Planalto nesta quarta, Lula disse aos jovens presentes que eles precisam se organizar para evitar a perda de conquistas sociais.

"Se preparem, porque fazer é difícil, para destruir, é apenas um passo. É um passo. Então, se organizem, para que vocês não permitam que ninguém tire o que vocês conquistaram. Porque vocês sabem que tem maluco pra tudo. Não é só maluco beleza, tem maluco pra tudo", disse Lula.

"E o cara pode entrar e falar: 'Não gosto disso, não presta, vai ensinar bobagem para o meu filho, porque quero uma escolha cívico-militar, porque eu não quero banheiro unissex'. Ou seja, essas loucuras que a gente pensava que não existiam mais, mas que existem. Então, agora, que vocês estão felizes e conquistaram a regulamentação, tirem proveito e façam disso uma grande indústria", completou.

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) experimentou um game brasileiro antes de assinar decreto que regulamenta Marco Legal dos Jogos Eletrônicos — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert

A legislação foi aprovada pelo Congresso Nacional em abril de 2024 e sancionada por Lula naquele mesmo ano, mas ainda precisava ser regulamentada pelo governo.

A lei estabelece regras para a fabricação, desenvolvimento e a comercialização de jogos eletrônicos no Brasil, além de prever incentivos para o setor.

Entre as medidas, está a possibilidade de empresas de games captarem recursos por meio dos mecanismos de incentivo fiscal da Lei Rouanet, destinada ao financiamento de projetos culturais.

Antes da assinatura do decreto, Lula se reuniu com gamers no Palácio do Planalto e chegou a experimentar o jogo brasileiro Árida.

Com a regulamentação, o governo fixou diretrizes para fomentar o setor de games, proteger a propriedade intelectual e os usuários, além de criar a plataforma pública Game Brasil para catalogar, promover e divulgar os jogos nacionais e indicar onde estão disponíveis.

Para fortalecer a produção e a inovação no setor, foram anunciadas medidas financeiras, incluindo a proposta da Ancine de reduzir o valor mínimo de empréstimos do Fundo Setorial do Audiovisual para R$ 150 mil e abaixar os juros.

Adicionalmente, o plano prevê captações de recursos através da Lei do Audiovisual, a criação do programa Rouanet Games para patrocínios, e uma chamada pública da Finep de R$ 200 milhões voltada para startups e soluções inovadoras.

No âmbito da formação profissional, o Ministério da Educação criará graduações na área em cinco universidades federais, complementadas por iniciativas de capacitação do Ministério da Cultura e do Ministério de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação.

O decreto também contempla a proteção da saúde dos usuários e de menores, em conformidade com o ECA Digital, medidas de simplificação de importações e aduaneiras, e a instituição de um comitê interministerial e de procedimentos simplificados no Instituto Nacional da Propriedade Industrial (INPI) para o registo de propriedade intelectual

articles.title: Republicans take an ominous turn in their midterm campaign
articles.summary: Vice President JD Vance on Tuesday made a joke that implied James Talarico is gay.
articles.body:
The worse GOP midterm prospects look, the darker the rhetoric from top Republicans becomes as they single out Democratic candidates as weird, threatening and antithetical to what it means to be and look like an American.

President Donald Trump is mocking the name of Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and slandering him as a " jihadist ."

Vice President JD Vance on Tuesday made a joke that implied James Talarico is gay . Trump keeps claiming the Democratic Senate nominee is a vegan who is incompatible with the carnivorous Lone Star State. Talarico is now often seen pictured with a plate of meat.

The president has also revived his searing racially derogatory rhetoric suggesting that Haitians and Africans are invading key election states like Ohio.

And after federal officials searched the home of Somali-born Minnesota Rep. Ilhan Omar on Monday, he underscored concerns he's using executive power to target a political foe by questioning whether she had constitutional rights as a naturalized citizen "from one of the worst countries anywhere on the planet."

Trump's rhetoric is hardly a surprise, given the linguistic excesses of his presidential campaigns, yet it's still jarring to see such overt racial language delivered from behind a presidential podium.

Some insults are delivered with a smile, which may offer Trump and Vance a modicum of political cover and the chance to argue it's all part of the rough-and-tumble of the campaign trail in a polarized age. But that hardly makes maligning someone's race, faith, personal appearance and manner more acceptable, nor does it absolve an intellectually low form of politics.

Trump has been accused of prejudice for years — especially over inflammatory social media posts and fake and racist conspiracies he pushed over former president Barack Obama's birthplace. The president, in seeking to appeal to voters, has often implied some minority political rivals are incompatible with traditional American culture and values. His anti-immigrant rhetoric seems at least partially aimed at his most conservative base voters who the GOP needs to turn out in huge numbers to stave off a midterm election disaster.

The most obvious explanation for this ominous turn in the campaign, beyond Trump's propensity for such dark arts, is that the Republicans lack a better story to tell. Trump's approval rating is at 33% in the latest CNN poll of polls — a daunting number for an incumbent president three weeks from a midterm election. Polls show majorities of Americans blame the president's decisions for worsening their struggle to cope with the high costs of food, housing, gasoline and diesel. And the rush by Vance and Trump to red states where Republicans never thought they'd be fighting in the campaign's final stretch tells its own story.

Branding Talarico as a "freak," as Vance did in Texas on Tuesday, seems an attempt to distract from the struggling and scandal-plagued GOP Senate candidate — Attorney General Ken Paxton , who was Trump's personal pick for the seat.

It's politics 101 for party leaders to seek to disqualify rivals whom they can't beat on the issues. Trump's singling out of Muslim candidates parallels his conceit that Democrats are "socialists" and "communists." And if he can malign El-Sayed and Talarico, he'll be doing his party a service. The pair are locked in races expected to go down to the wire on November 3.

Trump is going harshly negative on El-Sayed, the former executive director of the Detroit Health Department. "I call him Mohammed," Trump said in Tennessee on Saturday. "Somebody said, 'His name isn't Mohammed' I'm the president, I can call him whatever the hell I want." On Monday night in Ohio, he added: "He's a jihadist."

It is of course legitimate for Republicans to highlight and attack El-Sayed's record. They want to draw attention to his claim that Israel was committing genocide in Gaza shortly after the October 7 attacks . Many American Jews — Democratic voters among them — balk at the term, even while mourning the tens of thousands of Palestinians killed in the Israel-Hamas war following the terror attacks that killed more than 1,200 people, mostly Israelis, in 2023.

But calling El-Sayed a "jihadist" — namely a radicalized terrorist who rejects democracy, suggesting he's aligned with groups like Al-Qaeda or ISIS — crosses a rubicon. It's obviously intended to frighten voters into thinking that the Democratic candidate is a terrorist and security threat. And calling El-Sayed "Mohammed" demeans him and insults the humanity and individuality of all Muslims.

More broadly, the president seems to be portraying the Michigan-born Democrat and anyone who shares his faith as un-American and unworthy of the political rights of every citizen. His tactics recall his still-incessant use of Obama's middle name, Hussein.

El-Sayed responded to Trump's deliberate mangling of his name by arguing the president's focus insults the intelligence of voters. "He knows my name is Abdul. He says it everyday," El-Sayed wrote on X . "But he's not just attacking me. He's attacking all of us. He thinks so low of us. He thinks he can use my name and my faith to distract us from the suffering his policies are inflicting on us at the pump, at the grocery store, and at the doctor's office."

Trump escalates offensive against Ilhan Omar

The president's rhetoric toward Omar, with whom he's furiously sparred for years, has similar apparent goals. He implies that the Minnesota representative is importing what he depicts as the anarchy of Somalia to Minnesota. "She's a disaster. She comes in from a country without laws, without police, without military, without — all they do is shoot each other," he said in Ohio on Monday. "They come into the United States of America and they tell us how to run our country. We're not going to stand for it. They drive up taxes. They drive up healthcare costs, insurance costs, childcare costs."

Minnesota welcomed tens of thousands of Somalis in the early 1990s when their East African country collapsed into violence. The administration claims the community is laced with violent criminals and widespread fraud centered in day care centers. Somali leaders say violent criminals are a tiny minority, and that Trump and Republicans are maligning them without justification .

The Department of Justice said it carried out an enforcement operation at the home of Omar, who is running for reelection. It is not yet possible to independently verify any evidence or accusations against her. Omar responded that Trump had smeared her for years and was now targeting her as a political enemy.

Trump's aides repeatedly deny that he is racist or guilty of racist rhetoric, pointing out that he holds events to mark milestones like Black History Month and that he increased his support among minority voters in the 2024 election. In February , then-White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt slammed "radical Democrats throughout the years who have accused this president falsely of being a racist."

Many Republican voters also claim double standards, pointing out that Democrats often speak in demeaning terms about conservatives and Trump's voters more generally — including those who adopted Hillary Clinton's phrase that half of them were in a "basket of deplorables" as a perverse badge of honor. Some senior Democrats have openly charged that Trump is a fascist.

But Trump and Vance are also intensifying a trend that animates the newly populist Republican Party: a tendency to make specific judgments about who can be considered an authentic American.

In the 2008 campaign, GOP vice presidential nominee Sarah Palin argued that "real America" was defined by small-town patriots and hard workers who lived in "pro-America areas of this great nation" — implying that those outside the heartland lacked legitimacy and pride in the country.

Those remarks seem tame by comparison to the vitriol that Trump ushered in, and her subsequent apology now looks like a historical curiosity.

articles.title: Trump’s Supreme Court emergency docket scorecard, by the numbers
articles.summary: President Trump’s administration has filed 42 emergency pleas to the Supreme Court since retaking the White House — surpassing the count from his entire first term. And it doesn’t look like he’s hitting the brakes any time soon. Just last week, the Justice Department asked the justices to stop a ruling favoring Democrats in a fight…
articles.body:
President Trump ’s administration has filed 42 emergency pleas to the Supreme Court since retaking the White House — surpassing the count from his entire first term.

And it doesn’t look like he’s hitting the brakes any time soon. Just last week, the Justice Department asked the justices to stop a ruling favoring Democrats in a fight over TV advertising rates ahead of the midterms.

As the count ticks higher, we’re taking a look at Trump’s scorecard.

The TV ad rate case and another one concerning transgender inmates remain pending. Four others were withdrawn, leaving 36 emergency cases with an actual decision on the books.

Trump has effectively won 28 and lost eight, according to The Gavel’s analysis. That’s a nearly 80 percent success rate.

None of those wins was unanimous, however.

The Supreme Court justices often publicly highlight that the majority of decisions on their regular docket, called the “merits docket,” are unanimous. The court frequently acts unanimously in low-profile emergency disputes, too.

But when it comes to the president’s emergency requests, the justices’ ideological lines are clear.

Here’s a look at the 36 decided cases by apparent vote count:

Disclaimer: A justice can dissent in an emergency case without disclosing it (sometimes called a “stealth dissent”). This is based on dissents revealed publicly.

The four unanimous decisions? One was moot, another was cleared out after the justices decided an overlapping case, and the other two were unanimous losses for the administration.

He can blame Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson for that. She’s the only one of the court’s liberals to have publicly dissented against him every time he’s won.

Jackson has made no secret of her detestation for the Trump administration’s emergency docket tactics. It’s the subject of a lecture she regularly gives while traveling the country, and in opinions, she has called her colleagues’ decisions “ Calvinball jurisprudence ,” “ hubristic and senseless ” and a “ Kafkaesque nightmare .”

The two other liberal justices, Sonia Sotomayor and Elena Kagan, are sometimes aligned with Jackson, but the duo didn’t sign onto that searing prose.

In a few cases, they haven’t noted a dissent at all.

Sotomayor didn’t in two of Trump’s wins: at early stages of lawsuits over cutbacks to temporary protected status and large-scale government layoffs.

Kagan didn’t in four: those two Sotomayor cases, plus a battle over probationary employee firings and a challenge to Trump ending a Biden-era parole program .

To be clear, Trump hasn’t always won. And some of his eight losses were sizable:

The justices declined the administration’s pleas to freeze nearly $2 billion in foreign aid payments; reverse a whistleblower office head’s reinstatement; block the return of Kilmar Ábrego Garcia after his mistaken deportation to El Salvador; greenlight the firing of the Federal Reserve’s Lisa Cook; block a lawsuit over immigration judges’ public speech restrictions; deploy the National Guard in Chicago; re-fire the nation’s top copyright official ; and, most recently, OK his mail-in voting plan for the midterms.

The Supreme Court’s emergency docket is not new — for example, the court has long considered last-ditch efforts to stave off executions — but it has surged in activity during Trump’s presidencies.

The president’s critics say his flood of appeals reflects that he is acting lawlessly. Trump and his supporters say lower judges stymying the president’s agenda are the ones at fault and are forcing the administration’s hand.

Regardless of who is right, emergency cases now dominate the court’s work.

So, let’s look at the scorecard for those lower judges. Trump’s emergency docket wins have stopped more than a dozen.

Four judges have seen it happen more than once. Most of them serve on the bench in Boston: Brian Murphy and Myong Joun , both appointees of former President Biden , and Indira Talwani , an appointee of former President Obama . Edward Chen , an Obama appointee who serves in San Francisco, rounds out the leaderboard.

Just four of Trump’s 28 wins pushed back on a district judge appointed by a Republican president.

That’s no surprise. After all, litigants are concentrating their lawsuits in favorable districts, which are frequently assigned to judges appointed by Democratic presidents, who have repeatedly ruled against the president.

Welcome to The Gavel, The Hill’s weekly newsletter unpacking the intersection of courts & politics from Zach Schonfeld and S ophie Brams . Email us tips at zschonfeld@thehill.com and sbrams@thehill.com . You can also reach out to us on X (@ZachASchonfeld and @sophiebrams) or Signal (zachschonfeld.48 and sbrams.32).

Trump ads blocked: The Trump administration was ordered by a federal judge in New York to immediately stop airing political ads featuring the president. A watchdog group, union and others have challenged the campaign as an unlawful use of government funds.

White House media ban : The Trump administration cannot bar CNN, Politico and MS NOW from accessing the White House while their lawsuit challenging the media ban continues, a federal judge has ruled

DOJ in hot seat: A federal judge in Washington, D.C., told Justice Department lawyers Monday that she was “furious” and “beyond disappointed” after hundreds of trees were abruptly cut down at East Potomac Park with less than a day’s notice. The judge has ordered a pause in tree removal through at least Oct. 26 while she weighs a longer injunction.

Trump’s triumphal arch challenged: The county of Arlington, Va., is suing the Trump administration to block construction of a proposed 250-foot arch in the nation’s capital.

Tupac murder mastermind sentenced: Duane “Keffe D” Davis has been sentenced to 40 years in prison after he was found guilty of orchestrating the drive-by shooting that killed rapper Tupac Shakur in 1996

The Justice Department’s Office of Immigration Litigation, which handles all civil immigration cases, has seen its caseload jump to record highs under the second Trump administration despite a dwindling number of attorneys. Our colleague Rebecca Beitsch took a look at the data.

Scrutiny surrounding the high-profile sexual assault investigation at Cornell University has intensified with the appointment of New York Attorney General Letitia James (D) as a special prosecutor. Our colleague Lexi Lonas Cochran has more .

White House press pool fight turns to antitrust

President Trump ’s longstanding feud with the media is escalating again.

The Justice Department announced over the weekend that it is opening an antitrust investigation into the country’s five major television networks after they briefly suspended pool coverage in solidarity with outlets that were barred from the White House.

The networks — NBC, ABC, CBS, CNN and Fox News — stopped providing shared video coverage of the president’s daily activities for several days last month in response to Trump’s decision to revoke the badges of CNN, Politico and MS NOW journalists.

Pool coverage resumed after a federal judge ordered access be immediately restored, but the White House has since barred CNN and Politico from fulfilling their duties, including aboard Air Force One.

A spokesperson for the Justice Department said it is examining whether the pause violated federal antitrust law, calling it a “group boycott among commercial competitors.”

The underlying legal principle is found in Section 1 of the Sherman Antitrust Act of 1890, a law passed during the peak of the industrial revolution that was intended to curb anti-competitive practices and rein in monopolies.

It reads, in part: “Every contract, combination in the form of trust or otherwise, or conspiracy, in restraint of trade or commerce among the several States, or with foreign nations, is declared to be illegal.”

Federal agencies like the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) assert that group boycotts can become illegal when they are used to fix prices, restrict or disadvantage competition or jointly target a certain entity.

“Any company may, on its own, refuse to do business with another firm, but an agreement among competitors not to do business with targeted individuals or businesses may be an illegal boycott, especially if the group of competitors working together has market power,” FTC guidance states.

The distinction has been heavily parsed in the courts.

In a landmark 1911 Supreme Court case called Standard Oil Co. of New Jersey v. United States, the court interpreted the Sherman Act to prohibit only unreasonable or undue restraints of trade rather than all restraints.

To determine whether the agreement crosses that threshold, the justices adopted a standard known as the “rule of reason.” It weighs the anticompetitive harms of a practice against its commercial benefits by analyzing factors like purpose and market power.

But courts have also treated some agreements as “per se” violations, which are so blatantly anti-competitive that they can be found automatically illegal without the balancing test.

It remains an open question how either approach could be applied to the pool coverage scenario, as courts have historically distinguished between economic boycotts and purely political ones.

The high court found in a 1990 case that a group of private lawyers in D.C. committed antitrust violations when they agreed to stop providing legal services to indigent defendants until the city raised their fees. Years earlier, the court concluded that a socio-politically-motivated, NAACP-led boycott of white-owned businesses in Mississippi was protected by the First Amendment.

The television networks have not publicly addressed the investigation but previously said in a joint statement that “no administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”

Cases the Supreme Court is taking up — or passing on — this term.

IN: DOGE, ‘material support’ for terrorists

The Supreme Court took up three new cases Tuesday. We previewed all of them in previous editions as ones to watch:

In U.S. Doge Service v. U.S. District Court for D.C. , the justices will consider the Trump administration’s efforts to stave off a judge’s demand that the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) turn over documents to shed light on whether it must respond to public records requests.

The high court on its emergency docket already sided with the administration at an earlier stage of the case. Now, they’re taking it up on their normal docket.

In Blanche v. Ozurumba, the court will review whether a Nigerian man’s cooking for a terrorist group while in captivity amounted to “material support” for the group, making him ineligible for asylum.

And in Berry v. United States, the court will wade into when criminal defendants bringing habeas petitions are entitled to appeal rejected arguments.

It’s a thorny issue, but it’s one that matters to Dave Clark , a former real estate executive commuted by Trump. He had a similar petition pending with the justices, which they’re holding onto.

OUT: Sotomayor, Gorsuch join forces on immigration

Last week, we told you to keep an eye on Herrera-Salazar v. United States .

A Mexican man was arguing it violated his double jeopardy rights to prosecute him a second time for illegally reentering the country while he was still on supervised release for the first conviction. That barred him from leaving U.S. soil.

The court turned away the man’s case, but it only came over a harsh rebuke of the government’s conduct from both a liberal and conservative justice.

Justice Sonia Sotomayor — an appointee of former President Obama — joined by Justice Neil Gorsuch — an appointee of President Trump — called it “ constitutional absurdity .”

“Because I hope the facts of this case are anomalous and because Herrera-Salazar has since been removed from the United States, I concur in the Court’s decision not to grant review in this case,” Sotomayor wrote.

Petitions for the Supreme Court to take up cases we are keeping a close eye on …

Roberto Clemente trademark: Puerto Rico made $15 million off license plates branded with imagery of baseball legend Roberto Clemente. His sons say it misappropriated his legacy and want the Supreme Court to reverse a partial loss dismissing some of their claims against Puerto Rico officials. The case is Clemente Properties, Inc v. Pierluisi-Urrutia .

Race-neutral admissions: The court has its latest opportunity to take up whether their decision invalidating affirmative action in college admissions also blocks schools from using race-neutral criteria to encourage diversity. The court previously turned away a similar case concerning a top-ranked high school in Virginia just outside the nation’s capital. Now, the issue has arisen on the other side of the city on the Maryland side of the border. The case is Association for Education Fairness, Petitioner v. Montgomery County Board of Education.

Sex offenders on Halloween: Missouri law requires convicted sex offenders to remain inside on Halloween, avoid contact with children, turn off outdoor lights and post a sign saying, “No candy or treats at this residence.” A man convicted of sodomizing a teenage girl — and later of violating the Halloween law — says it compels his speech in violation of the First Amendment. Missouri’s attorney general wants to revive the law.

Home distilling ban: Federal law makes it a felony to distill spirits in a home . The Trump administration appeals a ruling found it unconstitutional, rejecting the notion that the provision is necessary and proper for Congress to carry out its power to tax the beverages. A defendant charged in a different court, which ruled the other way, appeals in his case. The cases are Department of Justice v. McNutt and Ream v. Department of the Treasury.

The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments in Salazar v. Paramount Global , a case concerning whether the Video Privacy Protection Act protects consumers who subscribe to any of a company’s products or only those who subscribe to its audiovisual ones.

A federal judge in D.C. will hold a hearing in a lawsuit brought by the National Democratic Committee which seeks to block the Trump administration from using taxpayer money to fund political ads.

An evidentiary hearing is scheduled in the murder retrial of Alex Murdaugh , who is accused in the 2021 killings of his wife and son in South Carolina.

The Supreme Court will release an orders list with actions in pending appeals.

A federal judge in D.C. will hear testimony from Trump administration officials in a dispute over the removal of hundreds of trees in East Potomac Park.

A federal judge in California will hear arguments in a lawsuit from two nurses unions seeking to block armed immigration officers from conducting enforcement at polling places during the midterms.

A federal judge in Massachusetts will hold a hearing to decide whether to resolve the state’s challenge to Medicaid work requirements provision passed in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act without a full trial.

A federal judge in Washington will hear arguments as the Trump administration seeks to dismiss a lawsuit from 15 Democratic-led states over a Day 1 executive order declaring a national energy emergency .

articles.title: Social Security recipients will get a 3.6% bump in benefits in 2027
articles.summary: Senior citizens and other Social Security beneficiaries will receive a 3.6% boost in their monthly payments in 2027, the Social Security Administration announced Wednesday. It’s the largest cost of living adjustment since 2023.
articles.body: Senior citizens and other Social Security beneficiaries will receive a 3.6% boost in their monthly payments in 2027, the Social Security Administration announced Wednesday, making it the largest cost of living adjustment since 2023. Monthly payments for retired workers will rise by about $75 to an estimated average of $2,170 starting in January, the agency said. Nearly 72 million senior citizens, people with disabilities and others receive Social Security benefits. The roughly 7.3 million lower-income people who receive Supplemental Security Income, or SSI, will also receive a 3.6% bump. Some people receive both Social Security benefits and SSI. Social Security monthly payments are a key source of income for many senior citizens. That makes the annual adjustment “critically important,” Myechia Minter-Jordan, CEO of AARP, a powerful advocacy organization for older Americans, said in a statement. “There’s a lot on the line financially right now for older Americans: one in five have no retirement savings, and more people feel financially insecure this year than last,” she said. The annual raise “helps millions of Americans keep up with rising costs for groceries, routine bills, health care and other everyday expenses.” However, many older Americans say the annual adjustments, known as COLAs, haven’t been enough to cover their ever-rising expenses. Inflation has ticked up this year amid the ongoing war with Iran, which has sent gas and diesel prices soaring. But Social Security recipients only received a 2.8% cost-of-living adjustment for 2026. The COLA is based on an inflation metric from the third quarter of the prior year. A related metric, the Consumer Price Index, rose 3.7% in September compared with a year ago, the Bureau of Labor Statistics announced Wednesday. In 2023, Social Security beneficiaries saw an 8.7% increase, following the surge in inflation the year before. Part of beneficiaries’ COLA for 2027 will be eaten up by an increase in Medicare Part B premiums, which should be released in the coming weeks. The monthly premium for 2027 is expected to rise to $209.50, up $6.60 from this year, according to Medicare’s most recent trustees report. That’s much smaller than the nearly $18 jump in premiums for this year. Crucial annual raise Many senior citizens and their advocates have pushed for changes to the COLA to have it better reflect their actual cost of living. The inflation measure used to calculate the COLA is designed to reflect the costs for working Americans, not retirees, said Nancy Altman, president of Social Security Works, an advocacy group. Older Americans spend a larger share of their income on healthcare, housing and other necessities. “The COLA adjustment will help. But it doesn’t fully account for the costs that Social Security beneficiaries face,” said Altman, who supports switching to another inflation measure geared to spending by the elderly. Social Security benefits have lost 13.7% of their buying power over the past decade, according to a recent analysis by The Senior Citizens League, an advocacy group. Put another way, a dollar of benefits in 2016 is only worth 86 cents today. Payments would have to jump by nearly $296 a month, or about $3,550 annually, to restore their buying power for the average beneficiary, the analysis found. Others, however, would like to reduce the COLA’s generosity – particularly for better-off retirees – to help stabilize Social Security’s finances. Those collecting the maximum monthly Social Security benefit will enjoy a boost of more than $2,200 for next year, compared to a roughly $900 annual uptick for the average retiree, according to the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, a watchdog group. It noted that Social Security’s trust fund will be drained in six years, which will result in a benefit cut of 22%. “To help restore Social Security solvency, lawmakers should consider reforming future COLAs,” the committee said in a blog post. This story has been updated with additional information.
